title: Lithium-ion battery chain

chokepoint.physics: Electrode coating + cell assembly at scale — capital + process capability, ~80% China

eyebrow: Product-chain pilot · the cell in everything
h1: The battery metals are mined all over — the battery is made in China
deck: Lithium, cobalt and nickel come out of the ground in Australia, the DR Congo and Indonesia. But the battery is not the mine: it is refined chemical, cathode powder and an assembled cell — and each of those steps runs about 80–90% through China, whatever the map of the mines says.
byline: mine (spread) ≠ battery-grade refining (China) ≠ cathode/anode ≠ the cell ≠ the pack
correction: Securing the mines does not secure the battery. Lithium is mined mostly in Australia and Chile, cobalt in the DR Congo, nickel in Indonesia — but battery-grade refining, cathode and anode production and cell assembly are all ~80–90% China. And the recipe is shifting underneath: cobalt- and nickel-free LFP went from a tenth of EV batteries to about half in four years, deepening the midstream China leads rather than loosening it.

history.title: The recipe changed under the chokepoint: LFP share of EV batteries
history.note: IEA. Lithium-iron-phosphate cells — which use no cobalt or nickel — went from about a tenth of EV battery capacity in 2020 to nearly half by 2024. Three published anchors, not an annual series, so it is marked as an estimate. The point: even as the chemistry moved to escape cobalt and nickel, it moved toward a technology China leads (CATL and BYD), so the midstream chokepoint deepened rather than eased.

sections.h2: 1 · The mine is spread; the midstream is China

panels.h3: China's share down the battery midstream (2025)
panels.note: IEA. The mine map is genuinely multi-country — lithium in Australia and Chile, cobalt in the DR Congo, nickel in Indonesia. But everything between the ore and the finished car funnels through China: this is where the dependence actually sits, and it is not visible on a map of mines.

panels.text: Australia mines most of the world's lithium, but ships spodumene concentrate to China to be turned into battery-grade lithium chemical — China refines roughly two-thirds of it. The same pattern holds for cobalt and for graphite. Owning the mine and owning the refinery are two different things, and the second is the one that gates a cell line.

sections.h2: 2 · The recipe is changing under the chokepoint

panels.text: Lithium-iron-phosphate cells use no cobalt and no nickel, so they dodge the two most supply-constrained battery metals and cost less — and their share of EV batteries went from about a tenth in 2020 to nearly half by 2024. But LFP is a chemistry China commercialised and leads, so escaping cobalt and nickel meant leaning harder on the Chinese midstream, not less.
panels.note: IEA Global EV Outlook / Critical Minerals Outlook.

panels.h3: Why chemistry is a moving target
panels.text: NMC (nickel-manganese-cobalt) still wins where range and cold-weather performance matter; LFP wins on cost and cycle life; sodium-ion and other chemistries are coming. A supply analysis fixed to one recipe dates quickly — the demand for any single metal can halve in a product cycle, which is exactly why the atlas tracks the stage, not just the element.

sections.h2: 3 · Demand arrived faster than supply could

panels.h3: A market that reorganised in a decade

cards.d: The share of world lithium demand going into EV batteries jumped from ~15% (2017) to ~60% (2022). Batteries now ARE the lithium market.
Average battery cost fell about 90% from 2010 to 2023 — the enabling fact behind EV, grid-storage and much else in this atlas.
Makers cut cobalt per cell and moved to LFP to escape a metal ~65% mined in one country (DR Congo) — supply pressure, answered with chemistry.

trade_intro: BACI carries lithium carbonate/hydroxide, cobalt and nickel intermediates, and lithium-ion cells (HS 850760), but a traded cell's customs origin is the assembly plant, not the mine or the refinery behind it. Read the shares below as trading positions along a chain whose real concentration — the refining and cell midstream — is not separable in customs data.
